newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine car prices set to rise after peso fall.
newsitem.headline: Philippine car prices set to rise after peso fall.

text.p: Car prices in the Philippines were expected to rise after the de facto devaluation of the peso and most car firms were waiting to see where the peso settles before making pricing moves, automobile manufacturers said on Wednesday.

But despite the rising cost of importing cars as a result of the weaker peso, some automobile companies will be forced to absorb part of the impact as stiff competition makes it impossible to raise prices substantially, said Mario de Grano, secretary general of the Chamber of Automotive Manufacturers of the Philippines (CAMPI).
"At least 60 percent of a car's cost is imported," he said.
The peso plunged after the central bank said last Friday that it would allow it to trade in a wider range, a de facto devaluation.
On Wednesday, the peso opened at 29.50 pesos per dollar, down 11.74 percent from the average of 26.40 it was trading at before the central bank's announcement.
Honda Cars Philippines, a unit of Honda Motors, would wait until the end of this week to see where the peso settled before deciding on prices, said Arnel Doria the company's marketing chief.
He said Honda's existing prices were pegged at an exchange rate of between 26 and 27 pesos per dollar.
Florencio Jurado, senior vice-president at Toyota Motor Philippines Corp, a unit of Toyota Motors, said the company would assess its price strategy after two weeks.
"For every peso, it is a substantial increase in cost but we are still assessing the trend," he said.
Toyota and Honda are the biggest car manufacturers in the Philippines, together accounting for about 50 percent of the market.
Car industry officials said the peso's fall would make it difficult for them to achieve their targeted 12 percent growth in car sales this year.
Car sales had slowed down even before the peso woes began, latest figures from CAMPI show.
